jevspawn.branching.frontier: Select the integer return_value of the branch whose actual observed state best supports the original task goal within {remaining} remaining control rounds. Use the task rules, executed actions and returned observations. A stopped environment may represent failure; determine the outcome from its observation. The following operation can continue execution, revise the action declaration, submit, or discard a stopped branch. With zero rounds remaining, select the branch whose actual state best supports the final answer.
jevspawn.branching.operation:
Choose the next operation for the selected branch using its active declaration and the latest actual action-observation pairs below. A declaration with a reported native syntax or argument-format error needs revise so that subsequent values produce executable commands. A well-formed command rejected by the current environment state needs a different value combination through expand, unless the required command or value is absent from the declaration. A completed task supported by actual observations needs submit.

The initial empty declaration needs revise. Compiler rejection preserves any earlier valid declaration and supplies the exact error for correction. A valid declaration is reused by expand; revise replaces it while preserving the real branch state and history. Every nonterminal round with a valid declaration spawns actions and receives their observations, including a round that successfully revises the declaration. An empty declaration after failed construction executes no action. Remaining control rounds: {remaining}. A terminal branch whose observations report failure needs discard to continue from a retained branch. Submit a terminal branch when its observations establish the requested outcome.

operations.expand: Keep the active declaration and spawn actions from the current state using finite probability readouts; execute them and obtain real observations.
operations.revise: Construct or revise the reusable action declaration using the original task and current feedback. Compile the proposal and retain the acceptance or error as feedback. Then spawn from the resulting active declaration in this same round, if one exists. Preserve the real environment state and action history.
operations.submit: Produce the final answer from the selected branch actual state and observations, in the official answer schema, and end the task.
operations.discard: Discard this stopped branch because its actual observation reports failure, then continue from another retained branch.

jevspawn.branching.retention: After this choice, the runtime retains the first {width} branches in the model probability ranking, including the selected branch, and releases the rest. Expansion replaces the selected parent with its actual child states. Shared history preserves the observations already obtained, including observations from released branches; only the listed branch IDs remain available for execution.
jevspawn.branching.observations: Each branch contains its current_path, its latest complete action-observation events, and whether its environment stopped. current_path lists the events actually executed on that branch, in order. Other history events belong to alternative executions. Each history text_prefixes entry specifies a value path, an earlier event, and a line count: concatenate those initial lines of the earlier full string with the current suffix to recover the full observation. Resolve these references recursively. The latest branch events shown here contain their complete observation strings. return_value is the integer used to select that branch in this request. Historical event IDs identify past executions; return_value identifies the current selection.

Later decisions use those observations and branch histories to continue or submit the result. At construction time, define the reusable legal action components from the task rules; observations from future actions become available only after those actions execute. Construct a reusable one-transition structured interface from the original task and the public tool rules. The runtime owns JSON keys, types and reference syntax. Select the semantic construction option requested below. Preserve complete primitive action coverage; factor independent components into separate fields. Candidate fields describe one action, and repeated execution builds trajectories from observations. Construction limits and the complete partial declaration are supplied in state.
Current decision: {question}

jevspawn.declaration_builder.signature:
Fill the indicated string argument of the already selected tool. partial_declaration.action.tool identifies that tool, and DESTINATION identifies the argument being constructed. Your output describes the string value inserted at that destination; the runtime already owns the enclosing tool name and argument keys. Express this value as reusable parameterized native command signatures. The runtime will choose parameter values with finite GPU scoring, instantiate several commands in separate branches, execute them, and return the actual action-observation pairs. Later turns use that feedback to select states and act again. This call declares the allowed actions; no trajectory or solution is required.

Declare the reusable commands for one environment transition. Use the smallest executable transaction accepted by the public interface. When a command permits a sequence of moves, declare one move and let subsequent turns execute subsequent moves after observing their results. When the interface requires a joint tuple in one call, declare that complete tuple. Output one signature per primitive command form; the same signature is reused at every applicable state. Fixed native prefixes, separators, spacing and punctuation remain literally in the signature. Replace each variable component with a named slot whose complete finite domain is declared inline: {{name:enum("value_a", "value_b")}} or {{name:range(start, stop)}}. Here range uses integers with an inclusive start and exclusive stop. A required fixed-length string of adjacent independent characters uses {{name:repeat(count, domain)}}; The compiler treats every position independently. It allocates a field only when its domain has more than one value and concatenates all position values with an empty separator. Positions separated by spaces or other punctuation use separate named slots with those literal separators. The nested domain can be range(...) or enum(...). An explicit {{name:domain}} declaration binds that name to the stated finite domain. A later explicit declaration of that name with another domain creates a new binding from that point onward; earlier command forms retain their original bindings. A bare {{name}} inserts the most recent binding. Repeating the same name with the same domain reuses its field. Independent arguments within a command have distinct descriptive names even when their domains coincide. Different primitive command forms with different argument counts have separate complete signatures; a sequence of successive actions is executed across turns. Literal braces use doubled braces. These are Python Formatter slots with the stated domain expressions; the compiler generates all JSON containers and field IDs.

Declare complete primitive domains from the supplied rules and objects. Named slots occupy their actual positions in the native command, so this single declaration establishes their role and binding together. Parameters that can vary across future states belong in domains even when a particular value is currently inapplicable. Subsequent observations determine applicability and success.

The output consists of the signature lines themselves, with no surrounding string quotes, code fence, labels or explanation. An empty separator is represented by adjacent slots. Fixed whitespace is present literally between slots. Use repeated positions only for a joint value whose full length the native interface requires in one call. Each declared signature must fit the shown construction limits; the total field count includes only positions with multiple candidate values and one selector for each destination having multiple distinct command forms. A domain with exactly one value is a literal constant and consumes no variable field. The repeat count is bounded by max_array_items.

Active structured action declaration is active_declaration in the decision state. The fields and action template jointly define how finite value choices become one real environment call. Use the current branch state and observations for each value choice. The declaration can be revised by a separate control operation; revisions preserve actual execution history. jevspawn.state.format: This state uses shared tables to preserve every actual observation and field definition without repeating their text. An execution event with observation_id i has the exact observation value observations[i]. Each computed_values entry [i, value] binds the field described by field_definitions[i] to value. current_path gives the ordered events executed on this branch; current_feedback identifies its latest observation. Events outside current_path belong to alternative executions. Table indices are references, not scores or actions. All indices are zero-based. An event may contain text_prefixes: each entry names a value path and an earlier event. The text stored at that path is the new suffix appended to the full text at the same path in the referenced event. Reconstruct the full text recursively by concatenation. This encoding preserves the complete observation; the suffix shows the newly observed action and feedback without repeating its history. A branch declaration_feedback_ids list references declaration_feedback_records in order. Each index retrieves the complete original compiler feedback record, including acceptance, errors and proposed signatures. Repeated indices represent repeated attempts with identical feedback; they preserve their original order. This shared table preserves feedback content across branches.
jevspawn.state.frontier_format: Each candidate description contains its branch state, declaration reference, and latest execution_events with the exact action and observation value together. Shared execution_events contains the other events; observation_id i refers to observations[i]. execution_order gives the complete event order across the shared events and candidate events. Each computed_values entry [i, value] binds field_definitions[i] to value. current_path identifies the ordered events actually executed on a branch. Other events describe alternative executions. All table indices are zero-based references, not scores or actions. An event may contain text_prefixes: each entry names a value path and an earlier event. The text stored at that path is the new suffix appended to the full text at the same path in the referenced event. Reconstruct the full text recursively by concatenation. This encoding preserves the complete observation; the suffix shows the newly observed action and feedback without repeating its history. A branch declaration_feedback_ids list references declaration_feedback_records in order. Each index retrieves the complete original compiler feedback record, including acceptance, errors and proposed signatures. Repeated indices represent repeated attempts with identical feedback; they preserve their original order. This shared table preserves feedback content across branches.
jevspawn.state.history_format: Each execution event preserves its action, argument bindings, parent_feedback and observation value. A text_prefixes entry identifies a value path, an earlier event, and a count of complete text lines. The full string at that path equals those first lines of the earlier event's full string (including their original line endings), followed by the string stored at this event's path. Resolve references recursively. These references share identical text only; parent_feedback alone defines execution ancestry. The stored suffix contains the newly differing text. All original observation content remains available. execution_order lists event IDs in their original order. current_path identifies events actually executed on a branch; current_feedback identifies its latest observations. Each computed_values entry [i,value] binds field_definitions[i] to value; these zero-based indices are references. Declaration references resolve in declarations. bound_fields fixes choices for the current action. A branch declaration_feedback_ids list references declaration_feedback_records in order. Each index retrieves the complete original compiler feedback record, including acceptance, errors and proposed signatures. Repeated indices represent repeated attempts with identical feedback; they preserve their original order. This shared table preserves feedback content across branches.

shared.runtime_contract:
Runtime contract for this task: {contract}
The input limit applies to each complete request, including the task, history, and observations. The output limit applies to each autoregressive response. The time limit covers the complete task. max_turns limits serial action-to-observation transitions along each environment branch. Parallel child actions from one parent each advance to the same next depth. Declaration, model scoring, and summaries consume time but do not advance that depth. Final submission remains available at the transition limit. When branch_width and parent_width are present, the runtime retains up to branch_width conditional action combinations and expands up to parent_width parent states per execution round. Candidate capacity is the maximum finite domain size supported by the actual model interface. Respect these limits while solving the task; do not reproduce this contract in the answer.

jevspawn.controller.system:
Solve the assigned problem using the available computation runtime. The Question specifies your current responsibility; State contains the original problem and the results actually returned by prior computations. Evaluate the meaning and correctness of the supplied Options against that evidence. An action selection requests real execution by the runtime; a value or verification selection supplies one result to the dependent computation. The runtime handles parallel execution, caching, and structured output assembly. Do not simulate tool execution or treat an unverified proposed answer as an observed fact.
This call uses a finite return interface: reply with exactly one option label copied from before a colon in Options, then stop. The label conveys your selected computation or result; it is not a description of how the runtime works. Do not emit explanations, JSON, code, option descriptions, or surrounding text.
jevspawn.controller.output_instruction: Return exactly one displayed option label and then stop. Nothing else.

jevspawn.values.system: Select the actual values for the requested fields to advance the task using the observed feedback. The runtime supplies fixed JSON syntax. Your response is the ordered JSON array of field values, not option labels or explanations. A value may be a partial template containing unresolved ${field} references; choose that binding as a template, without pretending it is an executable completed action. Future fields will be selected separately.

jevspawn.action.system: Select the action object that best advances the task from the current observed state. The available objects instantiate the declared action template with the field bindings under consideration. Return exactly one supplied JSON object. The runtime supplies fixed JSON syntax. Remaining ${field} references are template bindings to be filled in subsequent field blocks before execution. current_action_observations contains the complete latest executed actions and their actual returns for this branch; use these observations as the current evidence.
